mbm-1376.clue: I’m the one turning the little crank.
mbm-1376.quote: For our play’s train scene I rotate a painted landscape behind the carriage window. I painted my grandmother waving beside one tree. She came to the show twice to catch herself going by.

mbm-1377.clue: I collect the tickets nobody tears straight.
mbm-1377.quote: At our old cinema the usher tears a different little mountain range into every stub. I glued a row together across the back of my film diary. My favorite comedy has the tallest peak.

mbm-1378.clue: I hid the harvest under the snow.
mbm-1378.quote: My winter quilt has a white flap for the vegetable patch. Lift it and there are rows of orange carrots beneath. My niece checks for them every time she spreads the quilt over her knees.

mbm-1379.clue: I use a shell to finish the edge.
mbm-1379.quote: I rubbed a leather glasses case with the smooth inside of a shell until it shone. My dad says it still smells of the beach. I think he means the dried sea lavender tucked under the flap.

mbm-1380.clue: I finished my first lift under a paper lantern.
mbm-1380.quote: The lights flickered off during our community gym’s open day. We opened the doors and hung lanterns. I waited until morning light reached the platform, then made the lift with paper flowers floating overhead.

mbm-1381.clue: Our golf balls have the same blue dots.
mbm-1381.quote: I mark my golf balls with blue dots for luck. Once a woman on the next fairway did the same. We played the rest of the round together and added a little smile to tell our balls apart.

mbm-1382.clue: I put a feather on the map.
mbm-1382.quote: The wind turned at a bend in the river and blew a feather into my kayak. I used it to mark the spot on my paper map while I ate. I know that turn now as the feather bend.

mbm-1383.clue: I found the quiet note on my paddle.
mbm-1383.quote: My kayak paddle drips a little sequence after each stroke. I slowed down until the last drop landed without a splash, then heard a kingfisher on the bank. I had been making all the noise.

mbm-1384.clue: I always check the empty wire.
mbm-1384.quote: A single swallow keeps returning to a telephone wire after the rest of the flock leaves. I sketched the last bird so often my notebook has a whole row of identical wires and completely different skies.

mbm-1385.clue: I take a portrait of the empty chair.
mbm-1385.quote: After family picnics I photograph the chair with the crumpled napkin and abandoned sun hat. My mother can name its occupant every time. The one with the orange peel is always mine.

mbm-1386.clue: I never wear matching socks on movie night.
mbm-1386.quote: My brother and I each pick a sock for who we think the mystery villain will be. At the reveal the winning sock gets waved above the couch. Our cat has learned to leave before the credits.

mbm-1387.clue: I like the hole behind the waterfall.
mbm-1387.quote: At our mini-golf course the little waterfall splashes my glasses whenever I lean down to line up a shot. I play that hole by listening for the plink off the far wall. It’s my best score.

mbm-1388.clue: Open the fan slowly and the whole dance floor comes back.
mbm-1388.quote: I took a paper fan to the club and passed it around our circle between songs. Everyone drew a little shoe on a different fold. The wobbly boot is mine. My friend kept moving my elbow to the music.

mbm-1389.clue: I pack a tiny forecast for my fingertips.
mbm-1389.quote: I painted a tiny sun, a cloud and raindrops on three press-on nails for a holiday trip. We saw all three weathers in one afternoon. By supper I was just pointing at the correct finger.

mbm-1390.clue: I keep my coat on until the first train appears.
mbm-1390.quote: I love railway films at the neighborhood cinema. The moment a locomotive fills the screen I take off my coat and settle in, as if I’ve found my seat on the train itself.

mbm-1391.clue: I’m training for the thimble cup.
mbm-1391.quote: Our tabletop mini-golf course ends at a thimble turned on its side. I carved a tiny putter from a broken ruler. Losing the ball in the carpet is officially a trip through the rough.

mbm-1392.clue: I crocheted a rescue net for marbles.
mbm-1392.quote: My nephew wanted a bag for his favorite glass marble. I made a snug little green net with a loop to hook onto his belt. Hold it in the sun and the marble lights up through each stitch.

mbm-1393.clue: My partner knows the waltz by my first footstep.
mbm-1393.quote: I practice a tiny tap before the music begins. Even across a noisy dance hall my partner can hear that tap and know where to find me. Then she holds out her hand and we begin.

mbm-1394.clue: I built a clock that forgets Sundays.
mbm-1394.quote: My little desk program showed a marching turtle counting the minutes. On Sundays I gave it a hammock. Now I check the monitor early just to make sure the turtle’s getting its day off.

mbm-1395.clue: I bought the sign after the sale.
mbm-1395.quote: A corner shop closed and everything went, including its wooden open sign. The owner sold it to me for a coin. I hang it on my kitchen door whenever I’m making a big Sunday breakfast.

mbm-1396.quote: I shaped a shallow blue dish like the puddle outside our back step and set a tiny clay bootprint on one side. The dish holds keys, though my nephew keeps bringing it pebbles from outdoors.

mbm-1397.clue: I listen for the table to begin.
mbm-1397.quote: Before our porch domino game my friends tap their tiles to call the neighbors over. An empty chair always appears from somewhere. I know the game has started when four different taps fall into time.

mbm-1398.clue: I draw the birds in pencil first.
mbm-1398.quote: I sketched a flock of starlings on a river wire, then went to fetch my ink. When I returned the flock was gone and the shadows had moved. I left them in pencil so they could still fly.

mbm-1399.clue: I changed the name of the trail.
mbm-1399.quote: The map calls it the old quarry path. After my little sister carried a windfall pear all the way to the summit we called it Pear Mountain. Everybody in our family knows exactly where that is.

mbm-1400.clue: I painted the washing line in the rain.
mbm-1400.quote: I liked how the empty clothespins hung against the gray sky. Halfway through, my neighbor clipped up a bright yellow raincoat. I changed my whole palette and started again.
